Subject: Redwood MSA redlines — liability cap & carve-outs

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking the call this morning. Per our legal team, I'm attaching Acme's consolidated redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (attachments: Acme-MSA-redlines.docx, OrderForm-v2.pdf). High-level asks on the liability topic:

- Liability cap should be "aggregate fees paid in the 12 months prior to the claim" (rolling 12 months).
- Acme prefers a multiplier approach only if tied to the prior 12 months; they do not want a contract-term total cap.
- Exclude consequential damages, but carve in (i.e., exclude from cap) direct costs arising from data breaches where Redwood is at fault.
- No carve-out for regulatory fines — Acme wants Redwood responsible for fines resulting from Redwood's processing errors.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on: (a) rolling 12-month fee basis vs. total contract-term sum, (b) whether we can accept an explicit data-breach carve-out, and (c) a recommended dollar floor (Acme wants a floor). They'd like a revised redline by end of next week.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to finalize internal approvals by 8/28.

Best,
Elaine
Contracts, Acme Analytics

Olga/Marissa — below are legal's recommended positions and two compromise language options we can present. I kept it operationally grounded and flagged the downstream implications.

Executive summary (short):
- Our preferred position: liability limited to the greater of $250,000 or 2x payments made in the prior 12 months (rolling). This balances predictability with exposure tied to actual spend.
- If Acme insists on a contract-term total, we should counter with a higher floor and a shorter multiplier (e.g., greater of $500,000 or 1.5x fees during term) — the term total opens us up if Acme pre-pays capacity.
- Data-breach carve-outs: we should NOT fully carve data-breach losses out of the cap; instead accept a limited carve-out for direct mitigation costs (reasonable forensics, notification, credit monitoring) when Redwood is grossly negligent or subject to a confirmed security failure. We should explicitly exclude regulatory fines and third-party claims for privacy fines from the carve-out.

Rationale and risk notes:
- Rolling 12-month bases align liability with recent spend and are easier for customers to model; downside is it can increase exposure if a customer ramps quickly.
- Contract-term totals are simpler but create perverse incentives around prepayment and multi-year discounts.
- Carving security incidents entirely out of the cap exposes Redwood to unbounded statutory/regulatory fines — unacceptable without insurance and explicit SLA triggers.

Proposed text snippets (pick one):
Option A (preferred — rolling annual multiple + floor):
"Liability. Except for liabilities arising from (i) willful misconduct or gross negligence, (ii) infringement of third-party intellectual property rights, or (iii) Customer's breach of confidentiality obligations, Service Provider's aggregate liability for claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (A) $250,000 and (B) an amount equal to two (2) times the Fees actually paid by Customer to Service Provider in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim."

Option B (compromise — term total):
"... shall not exceed the greater of (A) $500,000 and (B) an amount equal to one and one-half (1.5) times the total Fees actually paid by Customer to Service Provider during the Term of the applicable Order Form."

Security carve-out suggestion (narrow):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Service Provider's liability for documented and reasonably incurred direct mitigation costs resulting from a confirmed security incident caused by Service Provider shall be excluded from the cap, but shall not include regulatory penalties, statutory fines, or amounts that are contingent on third-party claims."

Ask for Sales: which option is acceptable commercially? If ACME will only accept a rolling 12-month construct, Option A is cleaner; if they're fixed on contract-term total we should push for Option B with the higher floor. Also confirm whether we can live with the granular security carve-out language above.

I'll add inline comments to the attached Acme redline doc this morning (tracked changes).

-Laura

Laura Bennett

Team — thanks Laura, helpful framing. Commercial take below.

Context: Acme's ARR today is material but they projected ~2.2x growth next 12 months with a big pilot. Procurement will push hard on the rolling 12-month basis. They also asked our CISO whether data-breach remediation costs should be carved out — CISO pushed back on full carve-out.

Recommended commercial compromise to test with Acme:
- Offer Option A language but move the floor to $500,000 (greater of $500k or 2x rolling 12 months).
- Accept the narrow security carve-out Laura drafted limited to documented mitigation costs, explicitly excluding regulatory fines.
- Add an explicit clause that if Customer materially pre-pays >12 months of fees at signing, Parties will agree in good faith to re-calibrate the floor (gives us protection against large prepayments).

Why: Moves the dollar exposure to a safer band while keeping the rolling construct Acme wants. The prepayment provision reduces the risk of a large term-based exposure.

If we present that on 8/18 with a short note explaining the rationale, procurement has room to take it to legal quickly. Can we lock the language today? Laura, if you sign off I'll prepare a tracked redline and send to Acme end of day.

-Marissa

Elaine — thanks for the redlines and patience. Internal alignment complete; below is the set of positions we'll propose back to Acme. We're offering a single clear counter to keep procurement moving.

Redwood proposed language (single counter):
"Liability. Except for liabilities arising from (i) willful misconduct or gross negligence, (ii) infringement of third-party intellectual property rights, or (iii) Customer's breach of confidentiality obligations, Service Provider's aggregate liability for claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (A) $500,000 and (B) an amount equal to two (2) times the Fees actually paid by Customer to Service Provider in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. If Customer prepays an amount representing more than twelve (12) months of Fees at the Effective Date, the Parties shall in good faith negotiate an adjustment to the floor within sixty (60) days of the prepayment."

Security carve-out (narrow):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Service Provider's liability for documented and reasonably incurred direct mitigation costs resulting from a confirmed security incident caused by Service Provider shall be excluded from the cap, but shall not include regulatory penalties or statutory fines."

We will send a tracked redline with the language above and inline notes explaining the prepayment carve-in. Laura attached comments in the redline (redline-comments-Acme-MSA.docx). Marissa will send the external redline to Acme 8/18 EOD unless we hear any changes.
